feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 3 (score 449) is the best measured design: sensors at y 0.07, wheel_track 0.09, 12 mm footprint. It gave the oval 20 of 20 finishes with max_error 0.025 and oscillation 0.21. Its s-bend reached progress 0.68 with 1.0 line losses, max_error at the 0.06 floor and oscillation 0.32. Iteration 4 (score 392) showed that the 16 mm footprint restores slalom line retention (1.85 to 1.2 losses) but costs oval finishes (16 of 20) and lowers slalom progress, so the 12 mm footprint stays. Your yaw-inertia change is a sound way to add turn response without narrowing the track again. Iteration 3 showed that narrowing to 0.09 raised s-bend progress, but the s-bend still hit the floor, so the rotational response is the next thing to test. Read the next race as follows. If s-bend line_loss_events fall below 1.0 and steering_oscillation stays under about 0.35 on the oval and s-bend, keep body_length 0.12 and mass 0.6 and move on to a lower-inertia step. If oscillation rises above about 0.35 on any track, the faster yaw response is causing jitter, so restore the body length first, since that keeps the mass benefit. If the s-bend stays at 1.0 losses with max_error at the floor and oscillation is low, the limit is turn authority, not inertia, and the next change should come from the controller.
requested_changes: If the s-bend improves (line_loss_events below 1.0, progress above 0.68) and steering_oscillation stays under about 0.35 on all tracks, try body_length 0.10 with mass 0.6, since iteration 3 showed the s-bend at 0.68 progress and this step lowers yaw inertia further without changing the sensor layout.

If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.35 on the oval or s-bend, restore body_length to 0.16 and keep mass 0.6, since iteration 3 gave s-bend oscillation 0.32 and oval 0.21 at the higher inertia, and the mass change alone should not add jitter.

If the s-bend stays at 1.0 line losses with max_error at the 0.06 floor despite the lower inertia, keep the geometry fixed at body_length 0.12, mass 0.6, sensor_size 0.012, and test a controller change (raise kd from 0.5 to 0.6, or lower kp to 2.5) rather than more geometry, since iteration 2 to 3 showed the s-bend is at its geometric limit.
